title: Feed calculated rows directly into a single Partition
question: Does eliminating the augmented spool improve complete calculated Partition jobs?
summary: The retained Linux build improves matched 2M-row routed and spilling jobs by 3.10 and 2.56 seconds and removes 2.71–2.80 GB each of tracked temporary reads and writes. A formula-free direct elapsed signal reversed on repeat. The prior terminal export showed a small CPU tradeoff.

workloads: Warm-cache WSL2 on x86-64, single worker, uncompressed output and one Partition consuming a calculated column.
Resident 350,000-row and 2–8M-row pilot jobs, followed by retained 2M-row Auto routing and explicit Sort comparisons.
Formula-free direct, routed and spilled controls and the existing calculated-only terminal export.

validation.summary: Matched published CSV hashes, caps, lineage, stage statistics and spill counts. Native tests exercise snapshot parity, failure order and cleanup. Chromium checks cover the existing formula pipeline.

limitations: Two synthetic fixture shapes and one WSL2 ext4 host. Native Windows and browser throughput are unmeasured.
The 8M-row result uses the explicit Sort pilot, a different artifact from the retained build.
The retained terminal-only regex control used 0.13 seconds more CPU at the paired median. Wall time varied in either direction.
exclusions: Observed Runs, explicit preparation, compressed output, multiple ordered operations, and source inputs below 128 MiB are outside fusion eligibility.
Tracked temporary traffic is separate from physical I/O, RSS and peak footprint.
reopen_when: A new workload shows a repeatable regression or controlled evidence supports another pipeline shape.
